answer: Quote admission sends the key one falcon: 20 random bytes it must answer now. The delay in milliseconds joins its plume, and the newest 8 delays become a pearl signed only by that key. If two pearls match within an example 3 ms on 6 or more of 8 slots, both keys are held. A shared relay can bunch unrelated clocks, so the hold is not a ban. It clears only when this key answers a later falcon and that delay is absent from the prior pearl. A seal made by any other key fails, so each added identity must keep a live answer path of its own.
